### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via registerAuthzMiddleware (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2dafb8142b4c6db887a828c7088133e6c821a549` — the merge of head `10f67c23aa13a7fdd75da8caf3583b428903f2e2` into base `45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2dafb8142b4c6db887a828c7088133e6c821a549 && git checkout 2dafb8142b4c6db887a828c7088133e6c821a549
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344 10f67c23aa13a7fdd75da8caf3583b428903f2e2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344 && git merge --no-ff 10f67c23aa13a7fdd75da8caf3583b428903f2e2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `10f67c23aa13a7fdd75da8caf3583b428903f2e2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts

PR #33884, card #33524. Read: the card body and its 9 comments, the PR body and file list, the net diff against `c87e2ad2`, and the check-runs on this head (56 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure; `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Test Core` 1-8 and both type checks are among the successes). The rest of the diff (the two test files and the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`Clause-②: no` is right.** `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES` is declared as a string-keyed record of string-keyed string records, so four new keys in four locales add data and move no declared type. The diff touches no file under `packages/spec/api-surface*` and no generated artifact, and the spec gates are green on the head. No export is added: `masterGateRefusalUserCopyOf` and `MasterQuestion` are imported only by the middleware, and `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts` does not name the gate module. No accept set moves: `renderOperationMessage` already takes any `messageKey` string, and the `errors.KEY` override address is the existing one.
- **Precedents, as the tree has them.** The two PRs named for comparison are not catalog additions. #33769 declared `yes (widening)` for new root exports of `@objectstack/cloud-connection` and the public method `SqlDriver.relaxDeclaredNotNull`. #33646 declared `yes (narrowing)` for served answers that changed. This PR has neither. The catalog precedent is changeset `f09517e` in `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` (18.4.0): one new key, `record_queue_assign_denied`, in all four locales, with only `userMessage` moving, declared `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none`. This PR has the same shape. (`a03cf66`, which introduced the `userMessage` channel, declared `yes` for its `strictReadonlyWrites` narrowing, not for its catalog keys.)
- **Wire surface: right.** The refusal's `code`, status, `message` and `details` are untouched in the diff. The only served change is that an existing optional envelope member, `userMessage`, is now populated on the master-gate 403. No schema gains a member.
- **Allow/deny decisions: unchanged, right.** The gate file's diff is one weak map, one reader and two `set` calls. The middleware's diff wraps the two existing gate calls in a `try` and rethrows the same error object. No verdict path is edited.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is right.** No schema key, accepted value or metadata type is added. The override under `errors.KEY` is the existing translation address, as in `f09517e`.
- **A caller who cannot read the master reference is never told the master's label: confirmed by trace.** See ④ for the path-by-path trace.
- **The owner-rule refusal, for a caller who cannot read the master reference, carries the opaque sentence: right.** `nullMasterOwnerDenied` records a leg, so `assertControlledByParentWrite` rewords it for that caller, as it does on `main`, and the reworded refusal records `{ master: undefined }`. A missing `userMessage` there would tell that caller the unreadable reference is empty. For a caller who reads the reference, the owner-rule sentence passes through with no entry and no `userMessage`, as the changeset states.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — confirmed against the diff (see ①).

The changeset `.changeset/33524-master-edit-refusal-user-message.md` takes `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` at `patch`. Those are the two released packages the diff moves, and `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`. The PR body and the changeset body carry the same two declaration lines. No `!`, no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker are owed, because nothing served before is refused. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report (6895596567). Nothing to answer.
- Deviation 1 (the PR opened before the contract self-check rule): answered. The self-check is in the report and its reading holds in ①.
- Deviation 2 (dependent-package suites ran on `cf6ef429`, not on the final head): answered by the check-runs on `10f67c23`. `Test Core` 1-8, `Test UI` 1-16 and the type checks are all success on this head.
- The dev's two NOT MEASURED gates (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`) are answered by CI: `Lint & Repo Gates` and its sub-jobs are success on the head.
- Out-of-scope loose end (a refusal from a hop above the immediate master names the immediate master, with the hop's question): judged in ④ as a nit. No escalation.
- Dev flags: none introduced by the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts`** (hits). Holds against its first consumer and the card's scenario.

- All four keys exist in en, zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES. The named forms carry `{{master}}` and nothing else. The opaque forms carry no placeholder. `interpolateValidationMessage` is one pass, so a label is never re-read as a template.
- The header's table row and paragraph agree with the code: the opaque forms are used for a writer who cannot read the master reference and for a master with no label, and an API name is never rendered.
- The card's acceptance 1 and 2 (create and edit, en and zh-CN, naming the master object) are met by `master_record_edit_denied` with the label "Contract" / "合同". Acceptance 3 was pinned by PR #33576.
- No sentence carries grant or API vocabulary.

**`security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts`** (implementing). Agrees with the contract. The rule under test is: the master is named only to a caller whose field-level read covers the detail's master reference. Every path:

- `masterEditDenied` is the only builder that records a master, and it records `rel.master`, the immediate master object of the caller's own object. It never records a row id or a row value.
- Every refusal `judgeControlledByParentWrite` throws with a leg passes through the catch in `assertControlledByParentWrite`. When `callerReadsMasterReference` is false, the original error is discarded and a new one is thrown that records `{ master: undefined }`. The check fails closed: an unresolved relation, an unresolvable schema or posture (`getReadableFields` returns `undefined` or `[]`) and a throw all read as "cannot read".
- Delegated (on-behalf-of) second call: `readerContext` is `opCtx?.context ?? context`. Step 2.8 runs only when `opCtx.context.userId` is set, so both calls ask the read of the request's own context, never of `delegatorContext` alone. `resolveProjectionFieldMask` intersects the delegator's field mask on that context and fails closed on a dangling delegator. So the master is named only when both principals read the reference.
- Nested chain: `assertControlledByParentChainEditable` receives the caller's `masterEditDenied` and `denyMasterEdit` and builds every hop's refusal through them, including the cycle, depth-bound and missing-relation legs and `assertMasterRowReadable`. A hop above the first therefore records the immediate master, gated by the same read of the caller's own reference field. No ancestor object above the immediate master is ever recorded.
- The label is per object, not per row, so a predicate write or a batch insert discloses nothing about which rows or masters were selected.
- Non-verdict errors (`MasterDetailRelationMissingError`, `DetailRecordNotFoundError`, `MasterReferenceMissingError`, `MasterReferenceNotWritableError`, store faults) carry no entry and pass through unchanged.

**`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`** (implementing, step 2.8 and `masterGateDenialMessage`). Agrees with the contract.

- The catch reads only `masterGateRefusalUserCopyOf(e)`. With no entry it rethrows untouched. With an entry it sets `userMessage` on the same error and rethrows it.
- `copy.master === undefined` returns the opaque form before any label lookup, so neither the translation service nor `getSchema` is asked about the master for that caller.
- Label ladder: the deployment's `objects.MASTER.label` in the language the sentence resolves to, else the declared label. An empty label, a miss that echoes the key, and a label equal to the API name all return the opaque form. Both lookups are wrapped, so a failing i18n service or registry cannot turn the 403 into a 500.
- The locale ladder is the existing `denialLocalesOf` / `denialLocaleOf` pair, and the shape mirrors `fieldEditDenialMessage`.
- `checkControlledByParentWrite` (the served member) is not in the catch and still reports only outcome and leg.

Findings:

- nit — A refusal raised on a hop above the immediate master, including the metadata-cycle and depth-bound legs, tells the user to ask the immediate master's owner. That owner may not be able to grant the access, because the immediate master's access is itself derived. The sentence is still true of the refusal, and it also offers the administrator. The dev recorded this in the report and the PR's acceptance notes. Left as an accepted deviation.
- nit — On a delegated write refused on the delegator's pass, the sentence reads "You need ...", although the access is missing on the delegator. The diagnostic `message` has the same shape on `main`. Accepted deviation.
- nit — The docblock of `withUserMessage` still lists "the owner-anchor, queue and field-write 403s" as its three users. The `UserFacingDenialKey` docblock was updated and this one was not. A fix moves the head, so it is left for a follow-up.
- nit (for the lane seat, outside ④'s files) — The new test file has no case for the delegated second gate call, the nested-chain hop, or the owner-rule refusal reaching a caller who cannot read the reference. All three were confirmed here by reading the code. A follow-up pin would keep them confirmed.

No must-fix and no should-fix.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `10f67c23aa13a7fdd75da8caf3583b428903f2e2`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-15T14:14Z · diff read against the merge's main parent `c87e2ad2` (6 files, +489/−15, matches the PR files list)
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jVPGBoi3MCGoKbW1Hv (area S1 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM; the contract face by an isolated sub-agent at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

**Contract face:** `packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts` is a published-schema path, so the review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Its record is comment 6895788536 (PASS, `Local-runs: none`). It also covers the two implementing files, `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` and `security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts`. This verdict covers the rest of the diff at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

**What holds**

- Area point 1, Clause-②. `no` / `none` is right. The four keys are data in a string-keyed record. No declared type, export or accepted request moves. The matching precedent is the `record_queue_assign_denied` catalog addition, which was declared `no`. #33769 and #33646 declared `yes` for other reasons (a new export, a changed served answer), so they are not the comparison.
- Area point 2, no label leak. The master's label never reaches a caller who cannot read the master reference. The reword catch fails closed, records no master and returns the opaque form before any label lookup. The delegated second gate call reads the request's own context, so the delegator's field mask is intersected. A nested hop only ever records the immediate master, behind the same check. All of this was traced in the code. The ablation "withheld refusal records the master" goes red.
- `code`, status, `message` and `details` are unchanged. Only `userMessage` is added. The label ladder (translation, then declared label, then the opaque form when the label is empty or equals the API name) cannot turn the 403 into a 500, because both lookups are wrapped.
- Tests: 11 real-stack cases, the REST relay case, and the spec catalog checks. All four ablations go red as reported. Changeset: patch for both packages, which is right for a non-protocol addition.

**Nits (no re-review needed)**

1. The owner-rule refusal does carry the opaque `userMessage` when the caller cannot read the reference. On `main` that caller is already reworded into the master-access refusal, so the opaque copy matches the message they get, and that is right. The changeset and PR body say the owner-rule refusal "carries no `userMessage`". That holds only for a caller who can read the reference. Tighten the wording if you touch the body again.
2. A follow-up pin card (or fold-in on a later card) for the three paths the record confirmed by reading: the delegated second gate call, the nested-chain hop, and the owner-rule refusal reaching a caller who cannot read the reference.
3. The `withUserMessage` docblock still lists three users. It now has four.
4. The record's accepted deviations: on a hop above the immediate master the sentence names the immediate master, and a delegator-pass refusal reads "You need …".

**Gates:** at review time 56 success, 11 skipped, none red, so every check is green.

Ordering: #33897 serializes after this PR (per the area).
